audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts the whys directly beside it in three rows: whys[1] says 'Level 2 stays skill' but the chart says Jax, whys[2] calls level 3 'a coin-flip' but the chart says Jax, and whys[3] says 'Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's' but the chart says Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart (Skill, Skill, Skill, Zaahen, Skill, Jax, Jax) agrees with the prose and with a 51.35% win rate over 2668 games — a lane that is honest farming early, dips at 4-5 into his short-trade window, and turns Jax's at first item.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2 and 3 corrected in both layers as one atomic group, phases[3].rating dropped to 4/10 and phases[3].why rewritten so the 4-5 row states his advantage instead of generic lane-control advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: His ultimate's cooldown is never given — the page just calls it 'Ultimate' and 'his big cooldown' — and whys[4] refers to an 'early-ult edge' that the numbers do not support.
audit.why: His R is 110s at rank 1, dropping to 80s at rank 3, and it heals him for a portion of the damage dealt. That is a long first cooldown, which makes 'commit on the gap' a genuinely strong plan rather than a slogan.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now names the 110s cooldown and the heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: His passive is absent from the entire matchup, and so is his W. The page never mentions that at full Determination he can revive, and never mentions that his W pulls you toward him.
audit.why: A revive changes every all-in decision a Jax player makes: you can win the damage race, use Grandmaster's Might, and still lose the trade because he stands back up with bonus Attack Damage. And the W pull on a 14s cooldown at 850 range is how he starts the fights the page tells you to avoid — Counter Strike dodges attacks, so it does nothing about being dragged in. Together with the Q recast knockup these are the three mechanics that decide the lane and none were on the page.
audit.corrected: The revive is now in dontsFull[1].d, replacing a filler line; the W pull and Q recast knockup are in whys[3] and early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json P text 'can revive', W cd 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 range 850 'pulls them toward him', Q cd 10/9/8/7/6 with knockup on recast

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization carries no anti-heal at all.
audit.why: Both his Q and his R heal him — Q on a 10s cooldown at rank 1 that heals on every empowered attack, R for a portion of damage dealt. Two heal sources in a five-slot kit is exactly the case Grievous Wounds exists for, and this is one of the few Jax matchups where the page omits it.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now calls for anti-heal early and says why.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json Q and R heal flags

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ultimate's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window: the W pull and Q recast knockup chip you before your all-in matures. Concede the chip war and reach 6 healthy.

edits.before: His big cooldown. E around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It is 110s at rank 1 and heals him — bait it, then commit on that gap.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: At full Determination he revives — win the burst and he stands back up.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Trinity Force  (the classic spike), then Sundered Sky; boots Plated Steelcaps.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Trinity Force, then Sundered Sky; boots Steelcaps. Anti-heal early: his Q and R both heal.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's — his Q poke and short trades exploit you before the E-plus-W all-in fully matures; do not take his chip war.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's — his 14s W pulls you in and the Q recast knocks you up before your all-in matures; do not take his chip war.

edits.before: The first three levels are honest farming — neither of you can force anything — and then 4-5 is genuinely his: Q poke and short trades chip you before your E-plus-W all-in matures, and his ult arrives early. Concede the chip war, take only full-combo exchanges, and reach 6 healthy; that is where your R's resists and on-hit burst pull the duel back to even.
edits.after: The first three levels are honest farming — neither of you can force anything — and then 4-5 is genuinely his: his W pulls you in on a 14s cooldown and the Q recast knocks you up, and Counter Strike does nothing about either, since it dodges attacks and not displacement. Concede the chip war, take only full-combo exchanges, and reach 6 healthy; that is where your R's resists and on-hit burst pull the duel back to even.
